battle.name: 宋平丁進之戰
battle.brief: 建炎元年宋室南渡，壽春人丁進在蘇村聚眾萬數起兵反宋，十一月圍壽春二十五日不克而退，後經東京留守宗澤招納；宗澤病卒後再叛，劉正彥與劉晏統三千精兵、會八百騎兵赴淮西，以五色旗疑兵迫其請降，終以誘斬收場。戰役中與希臘火一類銅管燃燒劑最接近的，是宋代攻城與淮上水戰所用的猛火油。

kit.name: 希臘火
kit.history: 配在銅管裡的燃燒劑。配方是帝國的機密，配方和船一起沉了。

countries: 這場戰爭是南宋朝廷平定淮北叛亂的內戰，交戰方大致分為兩面。南面是建炎元年的南宋朝廷：高宗趙構自南京應天府遷都揚州，江淮殘破，兵力多為潰散與新募之眾；東京留守宗澤坐鎮開封，在建炎元年年底把丁進招納為「京城四壁外巡」；朝廷另以御營右軍副統制劉正彥與劉晏率三千精兵征討淮西，御營都統制王淵則自鎮江府遣小校張青以五十騎兵收尾。北面是丁進所部：丁進為壽春（治下蔡，今安徽鳳台）人，原是有罪軍人，違罪逃回鄉里，於開封東南的蘇村聚眾萬數，面上刺六點或「入火」二字，自號「丁一箭」，攻城略地，先後與壽春守臣康允之、東京留守宗澤、淮西征討軍交戰。戰場四周還有金人與同期叛亂者的壓力：陳通、張遇先後在淮上起兵，金兵又已占據淮北，使淮南處於半失半得之間；丁進本人曾欲率所部回到江北與金人血戰，說明雙方在淮線上互有拉攏與對抗。
countriesEn: This was a civil conflict in which the Southern Song court put down an armed rising in the Huai River country, and the two sides may be set out as follows. On one side was the Southern Song government of the first year of Jianyan: Emperor Gaozong Zhao Gou had moved the capital from Nanjing (Yingtian Prefecture) to Yangzhou, the Jianghuai region lay wrecked, and the field armies were mostly broken men and fresh recruits. The Tokyo military commissioner Zong Ze, holding Kaifeng, took Ding Jin into service at the end of that year and gave him the post of Outer Patrol of the Four Walls of the Capital, while the court also sent the deputy commander of the Right Imperial Camp, Liu Zhengyan, with Liu Yan and three thousand picked troops against Huaixi, the country west of the Huai, and later on the commander-in-chief of the Imperial Camp, Wang Yuan, sent the junior officer Zhang Qing out of Zhenjiang Prefecture with fifty horsemen to close the affair. On the other side were Ding Jin's followers. Ding Jin was a native of Shouchun (the seat at Xia cai, modern Fengtai in Anhui), a soldier who had been absent from his colours after an offence; he went back to his own country, massed tens of thousands of men at Sucun southeast of Kaifeng, had six dots or the two characters 'entering the fire' tattooed on their faces, and called himself 'Ding the Single Arrow'. By sieging, by wintering in the field and by raiding across the river he turned a rabble of stragglers into a body of men that could be ordered about. All around the theatre, the Jin and the other revolts of the same time pressed in: Chen Tong and Zhang Yu had risen along the Huai in turn, and the Jin already held the north of the river, so the country lay half lost and half held. Ding Jin himself later asked to lead his men back north of the river to fight the Jin to the death, which shows that along the Huai line the two sides were at once courting each other and resisting each other.
people: 核心人物是丁進（？—一一二九年），壽春下蔡人，南宋初期軍事人物。他不是盤據一方的割據者，而是趁宋室南渡、淮南兵力空虛之際迅速聚兵的流民首領：逃回鄉里後在蘇村集眾萬數，以面刺六點、入火二字為記號，自稱丁一箭，靠人身烙記維繫隊伍，並以圍城、屯駐、跨境攻擊三種手段把散兵游勇變成可以調動的軍事力量。壽春守臣康允之是首當其衝的守將，他以賞發銀帛激勵將士死守，頂住二十五日圍城。招撫方的主力是東京留守宗澤，他延攬不肯附金的老臣宿將，把丁進收編為京城四壁外巡，使其部眾屯駐東京，說明南渡初期朝廷對淮北武裝力量的爭取與安撫並行。真正奠定戰局的是劉正彥與劉晏：劉正彥以御營右軍副統制統三千精兵、會八百騎兵赴淮西，見丁進兵眾勢大便採劉晏「五色旗疑兵」之計，改易旗幟、沿山往復、連日不絕，使叛軍不能判斷官軍虛實而罷戰請降。建炎三年二月，御營都統制王淵自鎮江府派小校張青率五十騎兵，誘斬丁進於江北，為整場平叛收尾。
peopleEn: The central figure is Ding Jin (d. 1129), a native of Xia cai under Shouchun and a military figure of the early Southern Song. He was not a ruler holding a fixed domain, but a leader of displaced men who grew strong in the short space of the Song court's flight south and the emptiness of Huai-north: after going back to his own home district he massed tens of thousands at Sucun, marked them with six dots or the two characters 'entering the fire' tattooed on their bodies, called himself 'Ding the Single Arrow', and held the disorder together by that mark of the body, turning soldiers who had lost their units into a force that could be moved. The officer who bore the first blow was the commandant of Shouchun, Kang Yunzhi, who distributed silver and silk to the garrison to hold the walls to the death and stood off twenty-five days of siege. The chief instrument of pacification was Zong Ze, the Tokyo military commissioner: he drew in armed men from the north of the Huai who would not serve the Jin, enrolled Ding Jin as Outer Patrol of the Four Walls of the Capital, drew his followers into the court's establishment, and moved them away from the Huai to garrison at Dongjing, so as to break up the social and geographical base on which they had formed. What actually settled the campaign were Liu Zhengyan and Liu Yan: Liu Zhengyan led three thousand picked soldiers and joined eight hundred horsemen at Huaixi, and seeing how large the rebel host was, took Liu Yan's plan of feigning strength with flags, changing the colours of the banners, marching up and down the mountain road, one colour and then another, without break for days on end, so that the rebels could not read the true strength or the true line of the imperial army, and finally gave up the fight and asked to surrender, their men being distributed among the various units. In the second month of the third year of Jianyan the commander-in-chief of the Imperial Camp, Wang Yuan, sent the junior officer Zhang Qing from Zhenjiang with fifty horsemen to lure Ding Jin and cut him down north of the river, which closed the whole affair.
kits: 本卡兵器是希臘火，即拜占庭裝在銅管中噴射的燃燒劑，配方屬帝國機密，配方隨載有它的船一起沉入海底，技術自此湮沒。它在本戰役中的位置是技術譜系的對照：與希臘火同類的灌裝式燃燒劑在中國稱為猛火油，即盛於陶罐或銅鐵櫃中、臨陣點燃後投向車船與城樓的器材，兩者同屬以銅管或金屬容器承載的燃燒劑技術分支，只是施放方式與配方細節不同。淮上戰事正需要這類器材：壽春為淮水要衝，丁進以舟船、柴草逼近城垣，官軍須以火攻反制，否則木構城樓與艙船都易被火船攻破。宋人關於猛火油的認識，多承自南北朝以來類書所引的舊文，北宋官修器械圖說一系仍收此類燃燒器材，可見宋廷對燃燒劑並不陌生；本役實際投入的還包括宋軍慣用的火箭、火藥箭與攻城器械，叛軍則以柴木、舟船與城柵構成可焚可燒的目標。除火攻器具外，本役的骨幹是騎兵與步卒：劉正彥部三千精兵、會八百騎兵，張青率五十騎兵執行誘斬，壽春城上則靠金銀帛賞賜維持守軍士氣。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card is Greek fire, the burning agent sprayed from a copper pipe in Byzantium; the formula was a secret of the empire, and the formula went down with the ship that carried it, so that the art was lost. Its place in this campaign is that of a comparison within the same technical family: the filling-type burning agent closest to Greek fire in China was called menghuoyou, an agent kept in a jar or in a copper or iron case, lit on the spot and thrown at wagons, boats and the timber towers of a wall. The two belong to the same branch of technology, a burning agent carried in a pipe or a metal vessel, differing only in the way it is delivered and in the details of its composition. Warfare on the Huai was exactly the sort of fighting in which such equipment was wanted: Shouchun commands the crossing of the river, Ding Jin brought boats and brushwood up against the wall, and the imperial troops had to answer with fire, for otherwise the timber galleries and the hulls of the junks were all exposed to the fire boats. Song men inherited their knowledge of menghuoyou from the older notices preserved in leishu of the southern and northern dynasties, and the official collections of instrument drawings that went into the Northern Song's Wujing Zongyao still carried this class of burning equipment, so the court was no stranger to it. What was actually used in this campaign besides fire was the Song standard of fire arrows, gunpowder arrows and siege gear, while the rebels offered brushwood, boats and stockades as things that could be set alight. The skeleton of the fighting force was foot and horse: three thousand picked soldiers and eight hundred horsemen under Liu Zhengyan, fifty horsemen under Zhang Qing for the killing stroke, and at Shouchun a garrison held together by silver and silk paid out as bounty.
tactics: 本役的戰術可以分成守城、招撫、疑兵三段。守城段是建炎元年十一月的壽春之圍：丁進率眾圍城，守臣康允之用賞銀帛激勵將士死守，圍城二十五日不能克而退兵，這說明以流民、潰兵拼湊的攻勢缺乏攻城器械與持久補給，遇上有守城意願、且守臣肯於用賞賜維持士氣的城池便難以速決。招撫段靠宗澤：他以東京留守的權柄延攬淮北武裝，給丁進「京城四壁外巡」的職名，把叛軍的指揮權收進朝廷編制，同時把其部眾調離淮南、屯駐東京，就地拆散其原有的社會與地理基礎。疑兵段是建炎二年十月的淮西之戰：劉正彥會八百騎兵抵淮西，見叛軍眾勢大，不敢正面硬撼，採劉晏之計改易旗幟——先造疑兵，令軍士分作五色旗，沿山路往復巡行，一色走完再改一色，連日不絕，使對方無法判斷官軍真實兵力與進攻方向，最終罷戰請降，部眾分隸諸軍。最後是建炎三年二月的收尾：王淵自鎮江遣張青率五十騎，以誘敵深入的辦法斬丁進，顯示朝廷對反覆叛變的將領已不耐煩，改用伏殺而非再行招撫。整體而言，這場平叛靠的是編制、賞賜與疑兵三者配合，而不是一次決戰。
tacticsEn: The fighting of this campaign divides into three parts: siege, pacification and feint. The siege was the blockade of Shouchun in the eleventh month of the first year of Jianyan. Ding Jin surrounded the city, the commandant Kang Yunzhi paid out silver and silk to hearten the troops to hold to the death, and after twenty-five days the city was not taken and the rebels withdrew, which shows that an assault raised from runaways and deserters, lacking siege gear and lasting supply, could not take a walled place quickly against a commandant willing to keep the garrison fighting with money and goods. The pacification was Zong Ze's. Using the authority of his post as Tokyo military commissioner he drew the armed groups of Huai-north into the service of the court, gave Ding Jin the title of Outer Patrol of the Four Walls of the Capital, and so took the command of the rebels into the court's establishment, while moving his men away from the Huai to garrison Dongjing, breaking up in place the social and geographical base they had been built on. The feint was the battle at Huaixi in the tenth month of the second year of Jianyan. Liu Zhengyan joined eight hundred horsemen at Huaixi, saw that the rebel host was strong, and would not risk a frontal clash; he took Liu Yan's plan and changed the colours of the banners, ordering the soldiers to carry flags of five colours up and down the mountain path, one colour finishing before another began, without a break over several days, so that the other side could not tell the true numbers or the true line of attack of the imperial army; in the end the rebels stopped fighting and asked to surrender, and their men were distributed among the various units. The last part was the closing stroke in the second month of the third year of Jianyan: Wang Yuan, the commander-in-chief of the Imperial Camp, sent Zhang Qing from Zhenjiang with fifty horsemen to draw Ding Jin in and cut him down, which showed that the court had no further patience with a commander who had rebelled twice, and preferred a sudden killing to another offer of terms. Taken as a whole, this pacification was carried through by organisation, by payment and by deception in combination rather than by any single decisive battle.
data: 可核的數字不多，但都出自同一份記錄。時間線方面：建炎元年（一一二七）高宗自南京應天府遷都揚州，陳通、張遇起兵之後，丁進違罪逃還鄉里，在蘇村聚眾萬數；同年十一月他圍攻壽春，圍城二十五日不能克而退。建炎二年（一一二八）七月宗澤病卒，丁進復叛，九月率眾攻淮西；十月劉正彥奉命率三千精兵，會八百騎兵至淮西作戰，以五色旗疑兵迫其請降，部眾分隸諸軍。建炎三年（一一二九）二月丁進請率所部回到江北與金人血戰，被朝廷視為再叛，遂由王淵遣張青率五十騎兵誘斬。兵力方面，叛軍聚眾以萬數計，守方是壽春一城之兵，討伐方先以三千精兵加八百騎兵赴淮西，收尾時只用五十騎兵，說明南宋初年能直接投入野戰的機動兵力相對有限，多倚重騎兵作奇兵。時間跨度自一一二七年聚眾起兵到一一二九年二月事平，前後約兩年零兩個月，中間經宗澤招撫一次反覆。
dataEn: Few figures can be verified, but they all come from the same record. On the chronology: in 1127, the first year of Jianyan, Gaozong moved the capital from Nanjing (Yingtian Prefecture) to Yangzhou; after Chen Tong and Zhang Yu had risen, Ding Jin went absent in disgrace back to his home district and massed tens of thousands at Sucun; in the eleventh month of the same year he besieged Shouchun and withdrew after twenty-five days without taking it. In the seventh month of the second year of Jianyan (1128) Zong Ze died of illness, Ding Jin rebelled again, and in the ninth month led his men against Huaixi; in the tenth month Liu Zhengyan was ordered forward with three thousand picked soldiers, joined eight hundred horsemen at Huaixi, and used the feint of the five-coloured banners to force a surrender, after which the men were distributed among the various units. In the second month of the third year of Jianyan (1129) Ding Jin asked to take his own force back north of the river to fight the Jin to the death; the court read this as the intention to rebel once more, and Zhang Qing was sent with fifty horsemen by Wang Yuan to lure him to his death. On strength: the rebels numbered tens of thousands, the defenders were the garrison of a single city, the attacking force first committed three thousand picked soldiers and eight hundred horsemen at Huaixi, and the killing stroke used only fifty horsemen, which shows how limited the mobile field force available to the early Southern Song really was, and how much it relied on cavalry for the stroke. The whole business runs from the mustering at Sucun in 1127 to the ending in the second month of 1129, a little over two years, with one reversal in between at the hands of Zong Ze.
cause: 起義的直接背景是靖康之難後淮南的權力真空。一一二七年初金軍攻陷汴京，徽、欽二帝北遷，朝廷主力與中央官僚系統在戰火中崩解；同年高宗自南京應天府遷都揚州，淮南一線處在金軍南下的鋒芒與南渡朝廷尚未鞏固的防線之間，郡縣守令或死或逃，編制往往只存其名。丁進本人就是這支崩解軍隊的一環：他原是有罪軍人，違罪逃回壽春鄉里，在開封東南的蘇村聚眾萬數，面上刺六點或入火二字，自稱丁一箭，以人身烙記把無編制的散眾編為互助武裝。同時，先後在淮上起兵的陳通、張遇已使朝廷明白江淮並非安寧之地，金人對江北的接觸又提供了一些武裝集團另尋靠山的誘因。南宋的處境因此格外尷尬：既要倚靠淮北武力守江，又不能容許淮北武力坐大，於是有了先招撫、後討伐、再以誘殺收尾的曲折處理。
causeEn: The immediate background of the rising was the void of authority over the Huai after the Disaster of Jingkang. In the first months of 1127 the Jin took Bianjing, the two emperors were carried north, and the central apparatus of government and the bulk of the court armies dissolved in the fighting; in the same year Gaozong moved the capital from Nanjing to Yangzhou, and the Huai line lay between the oncoming Jin and a southern court whose defences were not yet settled, while county magistrates and prefects were killed or scattered and the units that remained were often names on paper only. Ding Jin was himself part of that dissolving army: a soldier who had committed an offence and left without leave, he returned to Shouchun and massed tens of thousands of men at Sucun southeast of Kaifeng, tattooing six dots or the characters 'entering the fire' on their faces and calling himself 'Ding the Single Arrow', using the mark on the body to bind an unorganised crowd into a mutual-aid armed body. At the same time the revolts of Chen Tong and Zhang Yu along the Huai had already shown the court that the Jianghuai was not a quiet empty country, and the Jin's contact with the north bank offered such armed groups an inducement to seek another patron. The position of the Southern Song was therefore awkward: it had to lean on armed strength from the north of the Huai to guard the river, without allowing that strength to grow too large, and hence the circuitous handling of the affair, first terms of surrender, then a campaign, and finally a killing by ambush.
impact: 這場戰爭的直接結果是淮南與京畿一線的秩序重建。丁進部眾在一一二八年淮西請降後分隸諸軍，等於把一支成建制的淮北武裝轉為朝廷的編制力量；丁進本人兩年後被斬於江北，未能成為割據勢力，也未與北方政權合流，避免了一次新的內應。從更長的視角看，它只是南宋開國頭三年地方叛亂密集的一環——陳通、張遇、邵興、李成、鐘相與楊幺、苗劉兵變接連出現於淮上、湖湘與江浙，說明南渡朝廷對地方社會的編制能力薄弱，鎮壓叛亂往往依靠招撫與主將個人的威望，而非常備制度的運作。技術面上，這場戰役也確定了猛火油一類灌裝式燃燒劑在淮上攻防中的位置：燃燒劑用於火船與城樓的攻守，是拜占庭希臘火與宋代猛火油在同一條技術線上的兩端，前者以銅管噴射的配方見長且隨船沉沒而失傳，後者則以容器盛裝、施放簡便，在南宋的攻城與水戰中延續使用。兩者的共同點是：以可燃介質封存於金屬或陶質器具之中，臨陣點燃投向目標，靠的是瞬間的燃燒而不是爆炸的威力。
impactEn: The direct result was the restoration of order along the Huai and around the capital. After the surrender at Huaixi in 1128 the men of Ding Jin were distributed among the various units, which turned a formed armed body of Huai-north into troops of the court's establishment; Ding Jin himself was killed north of the river two years later, becoming no separatist power and joining none to the northern regime, so a fresh defection was prevented. From the longer view the campaign is one link in the dense chain of local revolts during the first three years of the Southern Song - Chen Tong, Zhang Yu, Shao Xing, Li Cheng, Zhong Xiang and Yang Yao, and the Miao-Li mutiny followed one another in the Huai country, the lake region and the lower Yangtze, showing how weak the southern court's capacity to organise the local society was, and that revolts were put down by negotiation and by the personal authority of a commander rather than by any regular system at work. On the technical side the campaign also fixed the place of filling-type burning agents such as menghuoyou in the attack and defence of the river: burning agents used against fire boats and timber towers are the two ends of one line of technology, with the Byzantine Greek fire at one end, whose formula, remarkable for the spray of a copper pipe, was lost with its ship, and the Song menghuoyou at the other, simple to handle in a container and continuing in use in Song sieges and river fighting. What the two share is this: a combustible medium sealed in a metal or earthen vessel, lit on the spot and thrown at the target, working by the suddenness of the burning and not by the force of an explosion.
result: 平叛經過三個回合。建炎元年十一月，丁進率眾圍壽春，壽春守臣康允之靠賞發銀帛激勵守軍死守，圍城二十五日不克，丁進引兵而退；同年冬，東京留守宗澤將丁進招納，授以京城四壁外巡的職名，引其部眾屯駐東京。建炎二年七月宗澤病卒後丁進復叛，九月率眾攻淮西；十月御營右軍副統制劉正彥與劉晏統三千精兵、會八百騎兵赴淮西，劉晏獻五色旗疑兵之計，官軍改易旗色沿山往復，連日不絕，叛軍不能辨虛實，罷戰請降，部眾分隸諸軍。建炎三年二月，丁進請率所部回到江北與金人血戰，朝廷以為他要再叛，御營都統制王淵自鎮江府遣小校張青率五十騎兵誘而斬之。戰事至此結束：叛軍首領伏誅，部眾被拆散編入諸軍，淮南線上的武裝衝突告一段落。這場戰爭沒有決定性的大會戰，勝方靠的是城池死守、朝廷招撫、疑兵惑敵與最後的伏殺一步步收斂，也說明南渡初期宋廷平叛仍以非常規手段為主。
resultEn: The pacification ran through three turns. In the eleventh month of the first year of Jianyan Ding Jin led his men to surround Shouchun; the commandant Kang Yunzhi kept the garrison fighting to the death by paying out silver and silk, and after twenty-five days the city was not taken, so Ding Jin withdrew. That winter Zong Ze, the Tokyo military commissioner, took Ding Jin into service, gave him the post of Outer Patrol of the Four Walls of the Capital and quartered his followers at Dongjing. When Zong Ze died of illness in the seventh month of the second year, Ding Jin rebelled again and in the ninth month led his men against Huaixi; in the tenth month the deputy commander of the Right Imperial Camp, Liu Zhengyan, with Liu Yan took three thousand picked soldiers and joined eight hundred horsemen at Huaixi, and Liu Yan brought forward the plan of the five-coloured banners, the imperial troops changing the colours of their flags and marching up and down the mountain road without break, so that the rebels could not read the true state of the field and stopped the fight to ask for terms, their men being distributed among the various units. In the second month of the third year Ding Jin asked to lead his men back north of the river to fight the Jin to the death; the court judged that he meant to rebel again, and Wang Yuan, commander-in-chief of the Imperial Camp, sent the junior officer Zhang Qing out of Zhenjiang with fifty horsemen to lure him and cut him down. There the matter ended: the rebel leader was killed, his followers were broken up and taken into the various units, and the armed conflict on the Huai line was closed for the time being. This campaign had no decisive general engagement; the winning side closed in step by step through a city that held out, an offer of terms at court, a feint that disoriented the enemy and a final ambush, which again shows that the early Southern Song pacified rebellion mostly by irregular means.
